children: Global money market funds have recorded their largest cash inflows since April 2020, pushing total assets under management to an unprecedented $8T, according to Bank of America Securities.

holding around 4.2%, these safe-haven vehicles are now generating around $330B in annual interest income, creating an incentive for investors to stay put, strategist Michael Hartnett wrote in the latest BofA Flow Show note.

Historical data comparing six-month changes in money market assets against the federal funds target rate shows that sidelined capital rarely exits cash funds on its own. Major drawdowns in cash reserves usually required aggressive monetary policy shifts—such as the Federal Reserve's quantitative easing programs in 2009 and 2020—or sustained, deep rate cuts.
Unless significant Fed easing arrives to erode short-term yields, capital is likely to remain locked away from risk assets like equities
and credit. "No rate cuts, no cash cuts," Hartnett wrote.
